title: Julia & Jason's Fringe 2026 Shortlist
subtitle: Edinburgh Festival Fringe · 7–31 August 2026 · curated to taste: drama, music, storytelling, magic and spectacle — strictly no clowns

shows.title: Cathy
shows.why: Elaine C. Smith returns to the Fringe after 26 years — a sharp-tongued widow confronting family secrets. The Traverse is the home of Punch-style new writing.

shows.title: Gameplay
shows.why: Doc-drama about Vasili Arkhipov, the Soviet officer who refused to fire nuclear weapons during the Cuban Missile Crisis.

shows.title: Prophets
shows.why: Psychological thriller: a Scottish researcher meets a religious cult controlling a remote British Overseas Territory. Wicker Man atmosphere.

shows.title: The Second Best School Shooting
shows.acclaim: Produced by Matthew Lillard & Adam McKay
shows.why: Darkly comic play about a real school shooting — hard-hitting in the Punch vein.

shows.title: Badgers
shows.acclaim: Bristol Old Vic / Theatre Royal Plymouth co-production
shows.why: A modern folk tale about a podcaster who digs up something sinister, with live music by Jakabol.

shows.title: Man or Bear
shows.why: Three women navigating persistent male violence, inspired by the viral debate; directed by Ursula Martinez.

shows.title: Mayflies
shows.venue: Rear Warehouse at Brown's of Leith
shows.why: Grid Iron's site-specific adaptation of Andrew O'Hagan's novel, performed in a former Leith metalworks.

shows.title: Mohan: A Partition Story
shows.acclaim: By Fringe First winner Niall Moorjani
shows.why: The writer's grandfather's Partition experience, blended with live music.

shows.title: A Trial – after An Enemy of the People
shows.why: Wagner Moura in a courtroom reimagining of Ibsen — the audience sits as the jury.

shows.title: Book of Shadows
shows.acclaim: From the makers of Fringe hit Space Hippo
shows.why: Occult mystery told entirely through shadow puppetry — for fans of The Ice Hole's lo-fi invention.

shows.title: Dracula: Lucy's Dream
shows.why: Wordless, life-sized-puppetry Dracula told from Lucy's perspective. Extraordinary stagecraft.

shows.title: Elf Lyons is The Woman on the Edge
shows.why: Your past favourite — theatrical show about love, riffing on Vertigo, Apollo 13 and Pagliacci.

shows.title: Kirsty Mann: Corpse
shows.why: Comedian and working doctor tells a real-life ghost story — the Adam Kay slot.

shows.title: Steve Burns: Alive
shows.why: The former Blue's Clues host on parasocial fame and internet mythology.

shows.title: Ahir Shah: Golden
shows.why: Cerebral, moving stand-up — storytelling with real substance.

shows.title: Amanda Knox: Cartwheel
shows.why: Yes, that Amanda Knox — stand-up about her wrongful imprisonment.

shows.title: Susie McCabe: Coming of Rage
shows.why: Glasgow favourite on the health crisis that hit her at 44.

shows.title: Mark Thomas: 40 in Stand-up Years
shows.why: Four decades of political storytelling — as close to spoken word as stand-up gets.

shows.title: Simon Amstell: I Love It Here
shows.why: In town for two nights only.

shows.title: Mr Chonkers: Work in Chonkers
shows.why: John Norris work-in-progress — one late-night one-off.

shows.title: Sh!t Theatre: Evita Too
shows.why: "Hilarious, shambolic" song-driven show about Isabel Perón — smart, musical, very Fringe.

shows.title: Salty Brine: How Strange It Is
shows.why: Acclaimed cabaret storyteller splicing Neutral Milk Hotel's In the Aeroplane Over the Sea with Anne Frank's diary.

shows.title: Tether
shows.why: Scottish-Korean co-production spanning three generations through folk songs, love letters and war stories.

shows.title: Blackbox
shows.why: Hip-hop theatre about Henry "Box" Brown, who mailed himself out of slavery. Great lunchtime slot.

shows.title: Baby Wants Candy
shows.why: A fully improvised musical from an audience-shouted title. Reliably joyous.

shows.title: Kristen Schaal: The Legend of Crystal Shell
shows.why: Comedy play with an original score — Schaal with her Bob's Burgers co-star John Roberts.

shows.title: The Galloping Cure
shows.why: New opera about the opioid crisis — the Punch end of the spectrum, set to music.

shows.title: Bernie Dieter's Club Kabarett
shows.venue: Underbelly's Circus Hub on the Meadows
shows.why: Weimar punk cabaret with sword-swallowing and fire-breathing. Raucous, not clowny — front rows get teased.

shows.title: Ben Hart: The Labyrinth
shows.venue: Palais du Variété, Assembly George Square Gardens
shows.why: Mind-reading and reality-bending with heavy audience involvement — for fans of the pickpocket show.

shows.title: Kevin Quantum: Invisible Force
shows.why: Big-gasp, science-flavoured magic — a strong alternative if Ben Hart's timing doesn't fit.

shows.title: 360 ALLSTARS
shows.why: Urban circus: BMX, basketball, breakdancing, beatboxing, drumming. Scratches the Mythos spectacle itch.

shows.title: Mythos: Ragnarök
shows.why: Norse gods, professional wrestling, hard-rock Viking soundtrack.

shows.title: Loud Poets
shows.why: "Fist-thumping, heart-wrenching" spoken word backed by a live band.

shows.title: Adding Up America: Solving the Race Equation
shows.why: Monique DeBose blending live music, storytelling and sharp social insight.

shows.title: Woodhill
shows.acclaim: Multi-award-winning (Charity Awards; Sheila McKechnie Change Makers Award)
shows.why: LUNG's verbatim dance-theatre about suicides at HMP Woodhill, made with bereaved families — the closest thing at this Fringe to Punch's territory.

shows.title: The Horse of Jenin
shows.acclaim: Fringe First winner · 5★ Guardian · Rolling Stone Top 10
shows.why: Alaa Shehada blends storytelling, mask work and stand-up: a Palestinian boy's resilience, told through a five-metre horse built from debris in Jenin.

shows.title: One Man Musical
shows.acclaim: Guardian's No.1 comedy show of 2024 · Chortle Best Show 2024
shows.why: Flo & Joan's gleeful spoof musical about a certain musical-theatre impresario, starring Edward Easton with the sisters playing live — "better than Cats".

shows.title: Tell Me
shows.why: Sadiq Ali Company (The Chosen Haram): Chinese pole and aerial circus-theatre tracing HIV across two eras. "Stunning, soulful, a total triumph."

shows.title: Ten Thousand Hours
shows.why: Gravity & Other Myths' acrobatic meditation on mastery and the 10,000-hours rule — big-hearted, family-friendly spectacle.

shows.title: James Rowland: Team Viking
shows.acclaim: 5★ Lisa in the Theatre · returning for its 10th anniversary
shows.why: A true story about giving his best mate a Viking funeral — a comic ode to death, friendship and the absurdity of life. Pure Adam Kay territory: storytelling with real substance.

shows.title: My Grandpa Doesn't Follow Me On Instagram
shows.why: Trans storyteller Yoz Mensch retraces a Cornwall-to-Highlands road trip with her grandpa. A trained clown, she uses the craft for character and physicality, not face paint — this is Adam Kay-style storytelling with real substance.

shows.title: John-Luke Roberts: What I Talk About When I Run About, Talking
shows.why: His first new show in four years: surreal wordplay and absurdist stand-up turned on his own health scares and mortality — an endoscopy at 11am on Remembrance Sunday. Weird comedy with real substance underneath.

shows.title: Bog Witch
shows.why: Bryony Kimmings back at the Fringe after seven years, on uprooting her family to a permaculture homestead. “Haunting and hilarious… a climate reckoning of both cosmic and quotidian proportions” — big-tech visual theatre with Lewis Gibson sound design that makes a storm scene startlingly visceral.

shows.title: Sam Nicoresti: Baby Doomer
shows.acclaim: 5★ The Telegraph · 5★ The List · Edinburgh Comedy Award Best Show 2025
shows.why: Angry, absurd and political stand-up built round a misgendering in a department-store changing room — “uproariously funny, life-affirming, dumb and insightful all at once”. Exactly the weird comedy with substance underneath that they go for.

shows.title: Circa: Wolf
shows.venue: The Lafayette, Underbelly's Circus Hub on the Meadows
shows.acclaim: 5★ One4Review · Scotsman critics' best of the 2025 Fringe · reviewed by The Stage
shows.why: Ten Circa acrobats moving as a pack — all instinct and trust — then exploding into gasp-out-loud lifts, jumps and aerials over Ori Lichtik's primal DJ rhythms. The purest hit of the Mythos: Ragnarök spectacle itch at this Fringe.

shows.title: The Pitch
shows.why: East Belfast, a football pitch resurfaced for GAA, and a border poll on the horizon — three teenagers argue out territory, culture and national identity in fast, funny dialogue. The politics is the drama, not decoration on it.

shows.title: Celia Pacquola: Gift Horse
shows.acclaim: 5★ Chortle; Most Outstanding Show, Melbourne Comedy Festival 2026
shows.why: Steve Bennett calls it the Rolls-Royce of stand-up — a gag every couple of lines, craftsmanship hidden under what sounds like conversation. Fast, dense, warm but never soft: the Gilmore Girls signal in stand-up form.

shows.title: Frankie McNair: Huge Ass Mindset
shows.acclaim: 5★ Chortle, 5★ Glam Adelaide; shortlisted for Most Outstanding Show, Melbourne 2026
shows.why: Defiance, not a trauma dump — Chortle calls it proud, powerful and hilarious, vaulting from harrowing to joyously funny. Unsentimental and absurd in the way they like, with none of the cosiness.

shows.title: Andrew White: What a Life!
shows.why: A show about three deaths that refuses to be maudlin — Steve Bennett notes every moment of sentimentality gets knocked back with a gag, for "hard, life-affirming laughs from a place of real heart". Storytelling with substance in the Adam Kay line, and the impishness keeps it well clear of twee.

shows.title: Jenny Gorelick: SORRY
shows.venue: The Studio, Monkey Barrel Comedy (Niddry Street)
shows.why: The vapid-Jersey-girl persona is a disguise for perceptive commentary on gender expectations — why women apologise for everything and men for nothing — and the hour darkens as it goes. Sharp, confident and unsentimental: the Katherine Ryan signal almost exactly.

shows.title: Cecily Hitchcock: Family Recipe
shows.why: A surreal storyteller doing 2000s Britain — New Labour optimism to the crash — and Fest singles out a bit built on 1940s film dialogue: fast, allusive, warm underneath, which is the Gilmore Girls signal. Brazen and high-status rather than charming-and-nothing-else; Katherine Ryan has flagged her too.

shows.title: A Ghost Among the Living
shows.why: Box Tale Soup frame four Poe tales inside a lecture by a scholar whose own dark secret unravels him as he speaks — an academic losing control of his own argument, which is a very Arcadia shape. Handcrafted puppets and masks doing murder and madness, commissioned off real archive research at UCLA's Clark Library. Gothic and unsettling, nowhere near twee.

shows.title: Kate Dehnert: Echo
shows.why: A breakup show with the sentiment burned off — Dehnert bills it as a third play, a third stand-up, a third rave, and Chortle calls it "relentlessly fast", swinging from fury to silly in a beat. Rage about being left, played as force rather than fragility: the Katherine Ryan register, and about as far from twee as the Fringe gets.

shows.title: Lara Ricote: INKLING
shows.why: An hour built out from the three Delphic maxims into a genuine argument about what it is to exist — a withering routine on atheists, a Buddhist parable acted out, people sorted into free-spirited "naked babies" and clothed ones. Chortle calls it thought-provoking and hilarious in the same breath, which is the Arcadia shape in stand-up form. Ricote describes herself as a clown, but this is philosophising at speed, not a clown persona piece — flagged rather than dropped.

shows.title: Bunny!
shows.why: Craig Manson's murderous aspiring starlet, told through Broadway parodies and a tonal pivot from bright opener to outright horror — a satire on the brutality of making it in the arts, from the man whose Instagram eviscerates arts-organisation nonsense. High camp, but sardonic rather than cosy: unsentimental bite in the Katherine Ryan register, with none of the twee. Cabaret character piece, not a clown persona show.

doNotReadd.title: Bigfoot Ripped My Dog In Half I Saw It
Mythos: Ragnarök
doNotReadd.reason: already seen in a previous year

doNotReadd.title: Garry Starr: Classic Penguins
doNotReadd.reason: 5★ The Stage, but the show is the Garry Starr clown persona itself — top hat, tails and flippers, physical stunts on classic novels. Clowning is what the show is, not a technique it borrows.

doNotReadd.title: Sammy J: Hero Complex
doNotReadd.reason: Marketed as five-star, but the actual Fringe 2026 notice is Chortle 3.5★ (Tim Harding, 8 Aug): "exuberant innocence and gentle laughs", an earnest dorky persona, "a dispatch from a blessedly less edgy era". Structurally masterful storytelling, but the tone is precisely the gentle/twee register ruled out.
